newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Premier says Russian economic reforms will go on.
newsitem.headline: Premier says Russian economic reforms will go on.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Friday there was no question of Russia abandoning its economic reform programme, despite President Boris Yeltsin's absence through illness.

"The West should not worry. Reforms are not stopping, it's just that we don't have much money. But the desire (to reform) is great," Chernomyrdin told reporters. "There have been reforms and there will be reforms. There will be no U-turns in Russia."
Many economists say reforms have slowed during Yeltsin's prolonged absences from the Kremlin.
The president, ill since before the second round of Russia's presidential election on July 3, had open heart surgery in November last year and was taken to hospital last Wednesday with pneumonia.
Doctors said on Thursday that his condition had "stabilised significantly", although they have given no date when he might be released.
The prime minister, a former gas industry chief, has taken on the role as the main guarantor of Russian economic reforms. He stood in for Yeltsin while the president underwent his heart operation.
